wiki-iran.standing: Daily reads of Wikipedia's article on Iran, an Islamic Republic of about 90 million people on the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz. The line shows when the wider world turns to look at the country.
wiki-iran.recent: Tehran sent Washington seven conditions for ending the war through Qatar, while a bill to leave the Non-Proliferation Treaty awaited the speaker. Trump said a decision on new strikes was days away, Central Command put the war's cost at $43.6 billion, and a UN mission accused the US of war crimes, citing a school strike that killed 157.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of light, sweet North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's traded oil is priced against. Importing countries feel it quickly in fuel, freight and inflation.
brent.recent: With the Strait of Hormuz closed by the Iran war, the Houthis seized Yemen's Red Sea coast, which threatened the detour route. Saudi Arabia's only Hormuz bypass pipeline then shut. Prices later eased on hopes for UN-week diplomacy, even though only 12 commercial vessels crossed Hormuz over a whole weekend.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate, the light, low-sulphur US crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for oil priced in America. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do the finances of shale drillers.
wti.recent: The US-Iran war over Hormuz drove the climb. First came explosions on Kharg, Iran's key oil export island. Then the Houthi blockade of Bab el-Mandeb, and the shutdown of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, its only Hormuz bypass, left both Saudi export corridors constrained at once. US diesel reached a record $6.31 a gallon.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, delivered at a pipeline hub in Louisiana. It sets what American power plants and homes pay for gas, and it anchors the cost of LNG that the US ships to Europe and Asia.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's energy news came from the Gulf: drone strikes shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, and China and India switched to coal and oil instead of gas. None of it accounts for this price, which is set by US supply and demand.

wheat.standing: A monthly benchmark price for a tonne of milling wheat, the most traded food grain in the world. Weather in a handful of exporting countries sets it, and the cost of bread in importing states follows it.
wheat.recent: US diesel set a record at $6.31 a gallon, a cost that reaches every tonne hauled and fertilised, and European crops came out of a summer of heat and drought. New work on early heat waves makes timing, not peak temperature, the variable that decides a harvest. None of it accounts for the price.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark for the grain most of Asia and much of West Africa eats. Indian export curbs and monsoon rains move it, and food import bills in poor countries follow.
rice.recent: The fortnight's rice news was local. A dry spell and unpredictable rain pushed back ofada rice production in Ekiti, and El Niño disrupted planting and water supply in Agusan del Sur. Neither reaches an export benchmark whose latest reading predates both.

copper.standing: The world benchmark price for a tonne of refined copper, the metal in power cables, motors and wiring. Chile mines the most of it and China uses about half, so it is read as a gauge of industrial demand.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in the deepest bond market in the world. Mortgage rates, corporate borrowing costs and the price of risk almost everywhere are set off it.
us-10y.recent: The Fed voted 12-0 to raise rates, and the stated cause was a closed strait: Houthi forces captured Yemen's port of Mocha, oil jumped, and Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call days before the decision. Tightening into a supply shock lifts the whole curve, and Washington borrows at the long end of it.

sp500.standing: Five hundred large US companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the standard benchmark for American shares, and pension funds and index trackers around the world hold it.
sp500.recent: A warning about AI from inside a company's own cap table set off a global sell-off led by chip stocks, which fell 8% as AI apocalypse fears went mainstream. Rising petrol costs pushed US inflation sharply higher in August. Bond traders built an extreme short betting on a Fed rate hike, and markets took the hike calmly once it came.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq stock market in the United States, weighted by market value. A handful of tech giants dominate it, so it trades as a bet on American technology and chips.
nasdaq100.recent: Chip stocks led a global sell-off, down 8%, as fears of an AI warning went mainstream, a day after Anthropic picked Nasdaq for an IPO that could reportedly raise $100 billion at $2 trillion. Days later Washington capped Nvidia's compute sales to China, which hits the index directly through Nvidia.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil a few weeks behind, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice first.
us-gas-retail.recent: Pump prices followed crude after Brent rose 22% in a week. Ukrainian drones kept striking Russian refineries until Trump told Zelensky to stop. US diesel set a record of $6.31 a gallon, and Saudi Arabia cut off October oil supplies to Europe, which tightened the same fuel market the US refines from.

natgas-ttf.standing: The benchmark price of gas delivered into the Dutch Title Transfer Facility, the virtual hub where most of northwest Europe's wholesale gas changes hands. It sets what factories and power stations across the continent pay, and LNG cargoes sail toward whoever bids highest against it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Europe's rush to refill storage ran into a shortage of LNG cargoes, pushing October futures past $1,004 per 1,000 cubic meters in Amsterdam, a level last seen in December 2022. The same cargoes are being bid away from Asia: China and India switched their power stations to coal and oil rather than pay, and Bangladesh committed to two new import terminals by 2030 to secure supply it cannot currently outbid.

vix.standing: Cboe's measure of how much movement options traders price into the S&P 500 over the next 30 days. It rises when investors pay up to protect against a fall, which is why it is called Wall Street's fear gauge.
vix.recent: The fortnight's headlines were dominated by an escalating Saudi oil crisis, with Brent crude breaking $100, and by a new strait crisis brewing in the Red Sea; none of it accounts for the gauge easing over the window.

fx-pkr.standing: The number of Pakistani rupees one US dollar buys. Pakistan pays for most of its oil in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and power tariffs, and the IMF programmes the country relies on track it closely.
fx-pkr.recent: Pakistan's strain ran through fuel: Saudi crude to Pakistani refineries stopped, Brent sat near $110, and the policy rate was held. Jamaat-i-Islami marched on Islamabad against the petroleum levy, protests Muhammad Aurangzeb priced at Rs120 billion a day. None of it moved the exchange rate.

fx-ngn.standing: How many Nigerian naira one US dollar buys, so a rising line means a weaker naira. Crude exports earn most of Nigeria's dollars, and the rate passes straight into the price of imported fuel, food and medicine.
fx-ngn.recent: Nigeria rejoined a bond index, a reclassification expected to draw $17.5 billion of foreign money that has to buy naira before it can buy the bonds. Inflation fell to 15.39% in August. Hajj pilgrims must pay by 26 September, nine months early, so they carry the naira's swings against the riyal until they travel.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker pound. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel, so the rate passes quickly into the price of bread and energy.
fx-egp.recent: Reporting from Egypt this fortnight covered detained parents in Sheikh Zuwayed, Nubian farmers refused permits in Aswan and Sudanese refugees facing deportation in Giza; none of it bears on the exchange rate.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira one US dollar buys, so a rising line means a weaker lira. Turkey imports nearly all of its oil and gas, so each step down feeds into fuel and food prices at home.
fx-try.recent: Ankara lowered its medium-term growth forecast, and Turkey offered to meet Saudi Arabia's military needs as Houthi attacks on the kingdom escalated. Neither accounts for the lira's path over the period.

fx-bdt.standing: The price of one US dollar in Bangladeshi taka. Bangladesh Bank manages the rate. Demand for dollars to pay for fuel and cotton imports is set against what garment exports and remittances earn, and the balance between them sets the rate.
fx-bdt.recent: The fortnight's Bangladesh news was about dollars the country will have to find, not the rate it pays for them: a $1 billion Islamic Development Bank pledge for domestic refining, and two new LNG terminals planned by 2030. Neither explains the taka's small drift.

fx-idr.standing: Indonesia's currency, quoted as rupiah per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rupiah. It rides on coal, nickel and palm oil exports and on foreign holdings of government bonds.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah weakened as Jakarta's fiscal management came into doubt. Purbaya learned by phone, mid-meeting, that he had been fired as finance minister and handed the post to Suahasil. Three days later lawmakers were debating whether to break Indonesia's 3% deficit ceiling, the rule that keeps foreign buyers in the country's debt.

fx-lbp.standing: How many Lebanese pounds one US dollar buys. The currency lost most of its value in the banking collapse that began in 2019, and Banque du Liban has held the market rate close to fixed since 2023.
fx-lbp.recent: Israeli shelling around Nabatieh, the demolition of Hezbollah tunnels under Ali al-Taher and the stalled talks over that ridge all fell in this window, and none of it moved the pound, which the central bank holds in place against this kind of shock.

fx-cny.standing: The number of yuan one US dollar buys onshore. China's central bank sets a daily fixing and lets the rate trade only within a band around it, so its moves carry policy intent and pass into the price of Chinese exports worldwide.
fx-cny.recent: Washington and Beijing opened talks in New York on tariffs, AI and critical minerals before Trump greeted Xi at Andrews, with their trade truce expiring November 10. Nothing reported ties the yuan's firming to those talks or to any central-bank move, so they are the backdrop to it, not its demonstrated cause.

fx-inr.standing: How many Indian rupees one US dollar buys, so a higher reading means a weaker rupee. India buys most of its oil abroad in dollars, so the rate feeds straight into fuel prices and inflation.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee weakened after Congress passed a sanctions bill targeting Russia that threatens India with tariffs, and oil from Russia made up over half India's July imports. New Delhi vowed a 'determined' response. Foreign investors then built a record 290,041 index-futures shorts, a wager on how exposed India is through its oil import bill.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais to the US dollar. It is Latin America's most traded currency and one of the standard gauges of appetite for emerging-market risk, in an economy that exports iron ore, soy and oil priced in dollars.
fx-brl.recent: Lula raised Bolsa Família payments 15% by decree, adding spending to the books before a vote. The campaign tightened around corruption cases on both sides — police opened a probe into Flávio Bolsonaro over film financing, and the Banco Master scandal spread through Brasília — while Washington labelled the PCC a terror group.

fx-mxn.standing: How many Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, and one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. It carries Mexico's exposure to US trade, remittances and interest-rate gaps; a higher figure means a weaker peso.
fx-mxn.recent: The fortnight's news from Mexico was a dispute with the US over water treaty deliveries and Spain demanding justice after a student was killed in Cuautla; neither accounts for the peso's weakening.

fx-eur.standing: The single currency of most EU members, run by the European Central Bank and quoted here as euros per US dollar. It is the second-largest reserve currency, and its dollar rate sets what Europe pays for dollar-priced oil and gas.
fx-eur.recent: The fortnight's European news was political, not monetary: the AfD won Saxony-Anhalt, the first far-right victory in a German state election since World War 2, and von der Leyen offered Canada an 'associate member' status that no EU treaty defines. None of it accounts for the euro's weakening against the dollar.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a higher reading means a weaker yen. Decades of near-zero rates made the yen the world's main carry-trade funding currency, and Japan pays for most of its energy imports in dollars.
fx-jpy.recent: The BOJ lifted its rate to 1.25%, a 31-year high, but the US Fed had raised rates two days earlier, keeping the gap wide, and the governor's 75-minute briefing failed to win over markets. Tokyo has also weighed steering the yen with pension fund money, a lever that sits behind its balancing act with Bessent.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles one US dollar buys, so a higher number means a weaker ruble. Russia's oil and gas export earnings and its capital controls set the rate more than open trading does, so sanctions tend to show up here first.
fx-rub.recent: Congress passed a sanctions bill whose secondary tariffs fall on the buyers of Russian crude rather than on Moscow. Its obvious target is India, where oil from Russia made up over half of July imports. Ukrainian drones also kept striking refineries around Moscow. Neither story lines up with when the rate turned, and neither explains the moves.

fx-zar.standing: How many rand one US dollar buys, so a rising line means a weaker rand. It is Africa's most traded currency, often used as a liquid stand-in for emerging-market risk, and it moves with the gold, platinum and coal South Africa exports.
fx-zar.recent: Washington's sanctions on South African officials came a day before the rand's weakest point, but Rubio's order named no individuals and nothing ties it to the currency. The fortnight's other South African stories, from data-centre protests to 129,000 Zimbabweans leaving since June, don't explain the move either.

btc.standing: The first and largest cryptocurrency: a digital asset with a fixed supply and no central issuer, traded around the clock. It leads the wider crypto market, and a growing number of listed companies and funds hold it.
btc.recent: The trough followed the collapse of the Clarity Act in the US Senate. The recovery came as agencies moved without the bill: the SEC gave tokenized stocks a five-year exemption and a US regulator let wallet apps skip broker rules. Corporate bitcoin buying fell to 5,900 coins over the same stretch.

eth.standing: The price of ether, the token that pays the fees for running programs on the Ethereum blockchain. Much of decentralised finance and many stablecoins settle on that network, so ether trades as the working asset of the crypto sector.
eth.recent: The fortnight's crypto news mostly pointed the other way. The Senate's crypto bill collapsed, and Bitcoin fell 5% with it. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission then began writing crypto rules without Congress and let wallet apps skip broker rules. None of this explains why Ethereum climbed.

paxg.standing: A token issued one-for-one against allocated London Good Delivery bullion, so its price tracks spot gold. It is how crypto venues hold the metal, and unlike the bullion market it trades around the clock rather than on exchange hours.
paxg.recent: Brent crude broke $100, and the higher oil price stoked bets on a September Fed rate hike — dearer money is the standard case against metal that pays nothing. Hong Kong pushed the other way, with John Lee weighing an expansion of the city's gold reserves and a bid to make it an international gold trading hub.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: Daily reads of Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence, the field building machines that learn, reason and generate text or images. It swells with product launches, safety scares and new regulation.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Governor Gavin Newsom ordered frontier AI labs toward a mandatory shutoff switch, and experts at a Washington hearing doubted claims for Pentagon AI that struck 13,000 targets in 38 days. A day later Trump announced an AI Force and called superintelligence fears a "hoax", as Gemini became the fourth AI model to breach real companies in testing.

wiki-russia.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Russia, the largest country by area and a nuclear power with a permanent UN Security Council seat. People open it to find out about the country behind a headline.
wiki-russia.recent: Ukrainian drones struck Moscow as Russia held its first wartime Duma elections, killing two civilians on the final day of voting in a campaign aimed at refineries. The same week Congress passed a bill letting Trump tariff buyers of Russian oil 100%, and India, where Russian crude was over half of July imports, stood most exposed.

wiki-china.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on China. A steady base of students and travellers sits beneath it, and it jumps when a summit, a crisis or a trade fight sends people to look the country up.
wiki-china.recent: Trump greeted Xi at Andrews after officials opened talks in New York that put AI and critical minerals beside tariffs, with a trade truce expiring November 10. Beijing also urged Washington and Tehran to "stay rational" over the Iran war. None of it dates to the late-August peak.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: How many people read Wikipedia's article on the Strait of Hormuz each day. The strait is the channel between Iran and Oman through which about a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, and most Gulf gas, leaves for Asia.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Drones shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the only route that skips Hormuz, while the Houthis moved on Bab el-Mandeb, so both Saudi export corridors were constrained at once and Brent went above $100. Only three vessels transited Hormuz on one Wednesday, and Iran has since sent its terms to Washington through mediators.

wiki-india.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on India each day. The world's most populous country draws a steady global readership, so a jump marks a moment when events there reached readers well beyond the region.
wiki-india.recent: India hosted a BRICS summit at which Modi held 15 bilaterals in 3 days, Congress passed a Russia sanctions bill that threatens tariffs on India's Russian crude, and a Pakistani warship collided with an Indian navy vessel. None of these falls on the early-month peak.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: The US-Iran war has cut the strait to a trickle: only 12 commercial vessels crossed over one weekend. Drones then shut Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, the only route that skips Hormuz. Meanwhile, Iran's terms for reopening the strait reached Washington through mediators, as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Houthi fighters took Mokha in early September and then Perim Island inside the lane itself, putting the Yemeni side of the strait under the control of a party to the war for the first time. Brent reached $109.50, Saudi crude deliveries to Pakistani refineries stopped, and Italy moved warships to escort its own ships rather than wait for an EU mission.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Houthi fighters seized Perim Island and with it Bab al-Mandeb, the Red Sea's southern gate that ships bound for the canal must pass. After a US official met them in Oman, the Houthis said only Saudi-flagged vessels remain targets, yet Saudi crude to Pakistani refineries has already stopped.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The news on this route's oil trade came from its Gulf end: Brent above $100 as the US-Iran war ran on, explosions on Kharg, and Iran's Strait Authority adding tankers to a non-compliant list aimed at their insurers. None of it has shown up as a break in the traffic through Malacca itself.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The fortnight brought US-China talks in New York ahead of a trade truce that expires November 10, and Trump greeting Xi at Andrews. None of it involved a closure, a military exercise or rerouting in the Taiwan Strait, and none of it explains the traffic.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Panama City cut the number of daily transits and began rationing water as El Niño strengthened. The Pacific anomaly reached +3.01°C on 15 September, and a drier rainy season leaves less water to refill the lakes that each ship's passage through the locks draws down.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: The only recent news that reached the waters this strait serves was a drone attack on Russia's key Black Sea port. Nothing reported explains why fewer ships are passing through.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: The Channel crossings in the news this fortnight were asylum seekers, 140 of whom reached Portsmouth from Normandy. Boats like theirs are not in the commercial vessel count, and nothing reported in the period accounts for its movement.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: The fortnight's shipping story was in the Gulf. Iran's Strait Authority updated its non-compliant vessel list and went after tanker insurers, a projectile hit a tanker off Khasab, and Saudi crude to Pakistani refineries stopped. None of it accounts for the traffic around southern Africa.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: The fortnight's reporting on the war was about Ukraine's drone strikes on Moscow and Russian refineries, and a US sanctions bill aimed at buyers of Russian crude. None of it mentions the strait, and none of it explains why the tracked traffic stopped.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index, which tracks every main-market company on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh. It is the Arab world's largest market by value and Aramco dominates it. It trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week.
mkt:tadawul.recent: In the window, the main news touching Saudi Arabia was the Houthi advance: they seized a key port and took control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, a vital shipping route. None of it was reported in terms of Saudi-listed companies, and none of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:bist.standing: The BIST 100 tracks the 100 largest companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only exchange. It is priced in lira, so its level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Days before the September trough, Ankara revised its medium-term growth forecast downward, writing the regional war into its own numbers. Drone attacks from Iraq targeting Saudi Arabia followed, and Turkey then offered to meet Saudi Arabia's military needs, drawing itself further into the Gulf's security.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Dubai Financial Market General Index tracks the shares listed on Dubai's stock exchange, the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking. It trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The fortnight brought the war to Dubai's doorstep. Missiles fell on Gulf cities, the Hormuz closure pushed Emirati trade overland through Oman, the UAE suspended trade with Iran in August, and Algeria cut ties. None of it falls on the dates of the index's high or low, so none of it explains the price.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI tracks the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the exchange in Kuala Lumpur. That exchange is the world's biggest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The fortnight's news from Kuala Lumpur was political, not financial: Najib won house arrest in the 1MDB case for $12.3 million, Malaysia invited Myanmar's leader, and reform of the Peaceful Assembly Act was delayed again. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:idx.standing: Tracks every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country. Commodity producers and the big banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: The index's retreat from its high came alongside a fiscal shake-up. Purbaya was fired as finance minister by phone, mid-meeting, and handed the post to Suahasil. Days later, lawmakers in Jakarta were debating whether to break Indonesia's 3% deficit ceiling, the rule that has long capped government borrowing.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225, a price-weighted average of 225 leading companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, compiled by the Nikkei newspaper. Asia's largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The BOJ raised its rate to 1.25%, a 31-year high, yet the dollar jumped above 157 yen and Tokyo stocks climbed: a weak yen lifts the exporters that dominate the index, and the governor's 75-minute briefing failed to win over markets. The Monday before, SoftBank slumped 13% as markets priced an AI slowdown.

mkt:hkex.standing: Hong Kong's benchmark stock index, made up of the largest companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese firms meet foreign capital, which makes it the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The period's main China news was diplomatic. Washington and Beijing opened talks in New York on trade, AI and critical minerals before Trump greeted Xi at Andrews, and a US-China trade truce expires November 10. None of it explains the index's path through the window.

mkt:sse.standing: Every stock listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's largest market. Foreign investors are largely kept out, so it moves on Beijing's policy signals more than on global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Trade talks in New York added AI and critical minerals to the US-China agenda days before Trump greeted Xi at Andrews, with the current trade truce expiring November 10. None of that explains the index's summer path, and none of the domestic policy moves it usually follows were reported.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index, covering every common stock on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, which makes it a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The fortnight's news carried SK Hynix asking Intel to build its memory chips in Ohio, Samsung trading jabs with Apple over the iPhone Duo, and North Korea firing two ballistic missiles from Wonsan. None of it accounts for the index's summer slide.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensex tracks 30 of the largest and most actively traded companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai. The exchange, founded in 1875, is Asia's oldest, and the Sensex is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: Foreign investors ran up a record 290,041 index-futures shorts. It was a bet against an economy that depends on imported oil while only a trickle of ships crosses the Strait of Hormuz. A new law threatening secondary tariffs over Russian crude hits the same weak point, because oil from Russia made up over half of India's July imports.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest companies on the Singapore Exchange, the city-state's main market. Banks and regional property firms carry most of its weight, which makes it the main equity gauge for Southeast Asia's financial hub.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's own news this month was a 64% rise in the prime minister's pay, SGX opening bitcoin and ether perpetual futures to U.S. institutions, and haze from Sumatra peat fires. None of it touches the banks and property firms that carry the index, so none of it explains the rise.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange Capitalization Weighted Stock Index, covering the listed common shares on the exchange in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's reporting on Taiwan was diplomatic rather than commercial: a rare vice-presidential trip to Europe for a democracy conference, and a Lithuanian laser industry whose components a fab cannot run without. None of it accounts for what the index did.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It moves with tourism flows and with regional energy prices.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSE Composite Index: 30 of the largest, most traded companies on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila. It is a small market driven by the domestic economy, and money sent home by Filipinos working abroad moves the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The fortnight's Philippine news was a ferry fire off Coron, a school shooting in Banga, Bangsamoro's first parliamentary election and an anti-graft court's arrest warrant for Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks. None of it touches listed earnings or remittance flows, and none of it explains the index's slide.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Miners and banks dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Interest-rate fears drove the slide. The index plunged to a six-week low in early September and slumped again mid-month on rate fears. The RBA governor then issued a grim interest rate warning, and the Reserve Bank admitted it had never modelled what cuts to government spending would do to the path of imported inflation.

mkt:jse.standing: The FTSE/JSE All Share index, which tracks nearly every eligible company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in South Africa. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the continent's only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: South Africa's economy contracted for a quarter as the oil price fed through into output. Separately, the US put visa restrictions on South African officials and promised more sanctions over Pretoria's policies, and Pretoria answered that its policies had been misrepresented. Nothing reported links either event to the index's moves.

mkt:b3.standing: The benchmark index of B3 in São Paulo, tracking the most heavily traded shares on Brazil's only stock exchange and the largest in Latin America. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it.
mkt:b3.recent: Brazil is heading into a presidential election that has tightened, and the campaign has started to reach the market directly: Lula raised Bolsa Família payments by 15% by decree, spending that lands before the vote. Police opened a corruption probe into Flávio Bolsonaro over film financing, and Washington's terror listing of the PCC has reshaped the security argument the race is being fought on.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones: about 35 of the most traded companies on the Mexican Stock Exchange in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, and it moves closely with US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: Mexico's news in these weeks was a dispute with the US over water treaty deliveries, a femicide case in Cuautla and Chinese hackers breaching Latin American governments. None of it explains why the index fell.

mkt:byma.standing: The main index of the Buenos Aires stock exchange, tracking the most heavily traded companies listed in Argentina. Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years — direction over a day means something, the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: Argentina's monthly inflation reached a 14-month low in the August print published on Sep 10, the clearest sign yet that the disinflation programme is holding, and a slower pace of price rises pulls the peso-denominated index's mechanical upward drift down with it. Washington also approved a $103m Black Hawk sale to Buenos Aires on Sep 12.

mkt:tsx.standing: The S&P/TSX Composite tracks the largest companies listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market. Banks, energy producers and miners dominate it, so it trades more like a commodity index than a broad equity one.
mkt:tsx.recent: The fortnight was dominated by trade: the US banned Canadian dairy, alcohol and motorcycles outright, Canada's counter-tariffs on $20 billion took effect, and Trump threatened Bombardier by name, while the EU floated an "associate member" status for Canada. None of it is tied in the reporting to the index's path.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500: 500 of the largest US companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the biggest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The headlines of the last fortnight carried Apple's $1,999 Duo foldable, a slide in tech stocks on AI fears and a Fed rate rise. None of them falls on the dates of the summer high or low, so none of them explains the index's path.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies by market value listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a weaker pound tends to lift the index.
mkt:lse.recent: The one relevant thread in the fortnight was stagflation: Brent settled near $106 a barrel on Wednesday as bond yields climbed, squeezing economies that pay for imported energy. Nothing else in the fortnight's news, from airport disruption to Scottish independence talk, accounts for the index's path.

mkt:xetra.standing: The 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market, weighted by size. Carmakers, chemical groups and industrial firms dominate it, which makes it Europe's clearest read on export demand.
mkt:xetra.recent: German news in this window was about politics and interest rates, not company earnings. The AfD won nearly 44% in Saxony-Anhalt, Deutsche Bank raised its ECB peak to 2.75% on energy risk, and Volkswagen agreed to convert its Osnabrück plant to weapons work. None of it lines up with the index's turns.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest and most traded companies on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market. Luxury houses and energy firms dominate it, which leaves it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The Paris news of the fortnight was about defence and space: France's Future Combat Air System with Germany collapsed, and Europe awarded a cargo startup €760 million. None of it reaches the luxury and energy groups that carry this index, and none of it explains the slide.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The AEX, the 25 largest companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the main market of the Netherlands and the world's oldest exchange. Chipmaking-equipment maker ASML is by far its heaviest weight, so the index often moves with the global chip cycle.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The fortnight's news out of Amsterdam was about energy and the web rather than equities: October futures on European gas reached $1,004 per 1,000 cubic meters, and Cloudflare was shown carrying 9 in 10 European sites. Neither accounts for the index's path.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most traded companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its weight sits in banks with large Latin American businesses, which makes it a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spanish news in the window ran to the clashes as police cleared migrants off beaches in Ceuta, a parliamentary vote backing citizenship for Western Saharans, and Bit2Me's spin-off of a crypto-seizure firm in Madrid. None of it reaches the banks and utilities that carry this index.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest and most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main stock market. Banks and utilities dominate it, which makes it the equity market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight's Italian news was Meloni's pledge to ban niqabs in schools and Rome's decision to send warships to Bab al-Mandeb without waiting for the EU. Neither reaches the banks and utilities that make up the index, and nothing in the input explains its move.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index, the 20 largest and most traded companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The Kremlin moved by decree rather than through a court to seize Nestlé's Russian operations, and the company said it was weighing all options — a direct hit to the single heaviest weight in the index. In Zug, Bitcoin Suisse cut 60 Swiss jobs as priced custody work shifted to Bratislava.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The 30 most traded companies on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock market. It is heavy in Nordic industrials and telecoms, which makes it an early read on how much European companies plan to spend on capital goods.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The big domestic story of the fortnight was Sweden's election. The centre-left opposition bloc led 176 seats to 173 with 95% counted, which stopped Akesson's far right from entering government, and the Social Democrats got the first chance to form one. None of the reporting ties the result to the index's moves.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only public market. Banks, defence contractors and technology firms carry most of its weight, and it trades Sunday to Thursday.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: Daily reads of the English Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the 45th and 47th president of the United States. It is one of the most-read biographies on the site, so it jumps whenever his actions reach readers beyond the usual political audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Nothing reported from mid-September explains the early-month peak. That fortnight carried Washington readying sanctions to bar most transactions with the entire ICC, Trump greeting Xi at Andrews, three outlets barred from the White House, and a third House war powers vote, 220-204, as Trump weighed new Iran strikes.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily readers of the English Wikipedia article on the United States. It is one of the site's most-read country pages, so its baseline is high and it moves mostly around elections, national holidays and large crises.
wiki-united-states.recent: The fortnight's news out of Washington was dominated by the Iran war: Central Command told Congress it had cost $43.6 billion, and a UN mission cited US war crimes, including a strike that killed 157 at a school. The Fed also raised rates in defiance of Trump. None of it lines up with the late-August peak.

fed-funds.standing: The overnight rate the Federal Reserve sets for lending between US banks. It anchors the price of dollar credit everywhere — mortgages, corporate debt, and the emerging-market borrowing that is written against it.
fed-funds.recent: The Houthi capture of Yemen's port of Mocha pushed Brent toward $110, and the shock reached August consumer prices, which rose 0.4%. Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call days before the committee voted 12-0 to tighten — against a supply shock that no rate can undo, with borrowers paying for it.

ecb-rate.standing: The rate the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on funds parked overnight in Frankfurt, and the euro area's effective policy rate. It sets the floor under borrowing costs for 350 million people across the currency bloc.
ecb-rate.recent: An energy shock has turned the easing cycle around: Deutsche Bank now puts the ECB's peak at 2.75%, on second-round effects from crude that jumped past $105. The same closed strait pushed the Fed into a 12-0 vote to raise, and the Bank of Japan to a 31-year high, leaving the ECB the last major bank still holding.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of Americans in the labour force who have no job and are actively looking for one, measured by the Labor Department's monthly household survey. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates partly against it.

xag.standing: A digital token backed one-for-one by an ounce of vaulted silver, so it tracks the spot price. Industry, led by electronics and solar panels, takes over half of annual demand, so silver swings harder than gold.

us-cpi.standing: The year-over-year change in what US households pay for a fixed basket of goods and services, measured monthly by the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It is the number the Federal Reserve's rate decisions are judged against.
us-cpi.recent: Prices rose 0.4% in August, and the war has moved inside the index rather than sitting beside it. Expectations for US inflation are now being set against the Strait of Hormuz, so a shipping lane half a world away is reaching what American households pay.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: The daily count of tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz, read from ship transponder signals. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil and much of Qatar's LNG leave the Gulf this way, so a thin day here reaches fuel prices worldwide.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: The strait sits inside the US-Iran war: tankers pass under US escort, while Iran's Strait Authority keeps a list of non-compliant vessels and targets the insurers who cover them. A projectile killed one sailor off Qeshm Island, talks in Muscat were shelved, and drones shut the East-West pipeline, the only route for Saudi crude that skips Hormuz.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships passing each day through Bab el-Mandeb, the narrow strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa that joins the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. It is the southern gate of the Asia–Europe route through the Suez Canal.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Houthi forces took Yemen's Red Sea coast and the strait itself. After a US official met them in Oman, they narrowed their targets to Saudi-flagged vessels. Italy is sending its own warships to Bab al-Mandeb rather than wait for EU escorts, and Saudi crude bound for Pakistani refineries has stopped.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The daily count of ships through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea. Its southern approach runs through Bab al-Mandeb, so trouble there empties the canal and sends Asia–Europe cargo around Africa.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: The Houthis seized Yemen's Red Sea coast and a key port on the approach to Bab al-Mandeb, the strait every ship bound for Suez must first pass. Since then they have denied planting mines there and, after a US official met them in Oman, said only Saudi-flagged vessels remain targets.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: The number of ships passing through the Panama Canal each day, the lock-based waterway linking the Atlantic and Pacific across the isthmus. Its locks run on rainwater, so a dry year rations sailings for Asia–US East Coast trade.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: Panama's canal authority has been weighing further cuts to daily sailings as El Niño drains the lakes the locks draw on, with a new chief openly considering going below the level already set. The same forecast driving the rationing is projected to bring record drought to the Amazon. Separately, China opened the Pinglu Canal, removing a 560km detour for southbound cargo.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The narrow channel between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra, and the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most Gulf crude bound for China, Japan and Korea passes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news explains Malacca's own traffic. The shipping story was further west: only three vessels transited Hormuz on Wednesday, Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline shut, and the Houthis took Yemen's Red Sea coast, squeezing the Gulf crude that Asian importers buy at the far end.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: Ships per day through the Taiwan Strait, the channel between Taiwan and mainland China. It is the main lane linking the ports of northern China, Korea and Japan to Southeast Asia and Europe.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrow sea lane between Dover and Calais that links the North Sea to the Atlantic, and one of the busiest in the world. Ships bound for Rotterdam, Antwerp and Hamburg pass through it with much of northern Europe's seaborne trade.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: Ships passing daily between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean, the sea's only western gate. When the Suez route shuts, Asia–Europe cargo sails around Africa and enters here instead, so this count carries the Red Sea's detours.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The Houthis took over Bab al-Mandeb, closing the southern route by which Gulf and Asian cargo reaches the western sea lanes, and ships that avoid it come the long way round and enter through Gibraltar. Nothing reported ties a particular day's count to that diversion, and a reroute takes weeks to arrive, so the spike itself has no clear cause.

wiki-israel.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on Israel each day. It rises when the country's wars, diplomacy or politics reach readers who go looking for the background behind a headline.
wiki-israel.recent: A Haaretz report that the UAE warned Netanyahu of a Hamas plan days before 7 October drew a threat of legal action from him, while 12 countries including France and the UK moved to sanction trade from Israeli settlements. Washington then cleared 40,000 one-ton bombs for Israel, and Morocco agreed to exchange full embassies.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if US forces invade Iran before 2027, priced by what traders will stake on it. It turns on a ground invasion only, so air strikes and naval action alone do not settle it.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Trump said a war decision was days away, while Tehran sent 7 conditions for ending the war to Washington through Qatar, and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill went to the speaker of Iran's parliament. All of it concerned strikes and terms rather than ground troops, and none of it accounts for the price.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Ansar Allah, the Zaidi Shia armed movement that has held Yemen's capital Sanaa since 2014 and fought a Saudi-led coalition since 2015. Its reach over the Red Sea shipping lane gives it leverage over global trade.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Houthi forces seized a key port and Yemen's Red Sea coast, then turned on Saudi Arabia: drones shut the only pipeline that skips Hormuz, missiles hit King Khalid Air Base, and a ballistic missile flew at Riyadh. After talks in Oman, only Saudi-flagged ships remain targets under a "blockade for blockade" doctrine.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: The Gulf kingdom that holds Islam's two holiest cities, Mecca and Medina, and one of the world's largest crude exporters. Its output decisions and export routes set much of the global oil price.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: The Houthis took Yemen's Red Sea coast, a key shipping route, then sent the first drone toward Mecca since 2017 and claimed to have downed a Saudi jet. Saudi Arabia's only Hormuz bypass pipeline shut, and the Houthis declared "blockade for blockade" against Riyadh while sparing US ships.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Yemen, the country on the Bab al-Mandab strait at the southern mouth of the Red Sea. Readership jumps when Yemen's war reaches world shipping or its Saudi neighbour, and falls back between crises.
wiki-yemen.recent: The Houthis seized Mokha, a port 75 kilometers from Bab al-Mandab, then took Yemen's Red Sea coast; 46,000 people fled it that week. Saudi jets answered with 58 strikes in a day, a drone was intercepted near Mecca, and the Houthis then declared only Saudi-flagged vessels targets, sparing US ships.

wiki-openai.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on OpenAI, the San Francisco company behind ChatGPT. It rises when the lab's own decisions, not the AI field at large, reach a general audience.
wiki-openai.recent: OpenAI stood down an IPO it was weeks from filing, then said its model had solved Navier-Stokes before any referee had checked. Contractors were found reading real ChatGPT chats, an ad cookie tied accounts to advertiser websites, and the company disclosed six model incidents, one of which uploaded data to a paste site.

wiki-inflation.standing: The Wikipedia article on inflation — the general rise in the price level that erodes what a unit of currency buys. Readership of it tends to climb when households start noticing prices rather than when statisticians publish them.
wiki-inflation.recent: The Federal Reserve voted 12-0 to raise rates on 16 September, defying Trump's calls to cut, and the Bank of Japan followed two days later with a hike to a 31-year high. Behind both sits a supply shock: Brent near $106 a barrel with a strait closed, a 10-year Treasury yield at 5%, and a budget office estimate of $38 billion in five months of Iran war costs.

poly-will-delcy-rodrguez-be-the-leader-o.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Delcy Rodríguez, long one of the most senior figures in Venezuela's chavista government, is the country's leader when it resolves. The price is what traders pay for a share that pays out if she is.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Shares of Saudi Aramco, the state oil producer listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) in Riyadh. The government owns the vast majority of it, so the price moves with crude, the dividend and Saudi output policy.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: Houthi missiles set Aramco's Red Sea refinery at Jizan ablaze, part of a wave of strikes on Saudi energy sites that wounded 73 civilians. That put the company's own plants in the line of fire, not just the oil price it sells at. Saudi Arabia said it 'will not hesitate' to defend itself.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Daily reads of Wikipedia's article on Ukraine, Europe's second-largest country by area, which Russia invaded in full in February 2022. It shows how many people worldwide are looking up the country behind the war.
wiki-ukraine.recent: A drone hit a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland, and a NATO jet downed a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania. Trump asked Zelensky to stop hitting Russian refineries, but 350 drones struck Moscow as Duma voting opened, and a later attack on the capital killed two civilians.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still holding on November 30. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, to bet that it holds.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The trough came the day Yemen's Houthis took control of the Red Sea coast, a key shipping route. Since then traders have had two tracks to weigh: Iran sent 7 conditions to Washington via Qatar and its Hormuz terms through mediators, while Trump said a war decision is days away and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker in Tehran.

poly-friedrich-merz-out-as-chancellor-of.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Friedrich Merz stops being Germany's chancellor before the end of 2026. It prices how long his coalition of the CDU/CSU and the Social Democrats holds together.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Benjamin Netanyahu will be Israel's next prime minister. Its price is what traders pay on his political survival through coalition fights, his corruption trial and the next election.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: The fortnight's news on Netanyahu himself was a Haaretz report that the UAE warned him of a Hamas plan days before the 7 October attack, and his threat of legal action against the paper. Nothing in it explains what traders paid on his return.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States ends its blockade of Iran by 30 September 2026. Its price is what traders will stake on the blockade being lifted before that deadline.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Tehran has now put terms in writing, with seven conditions sent through Qatar and its Hormuz terms passed via Pakistan's mediators, but Washington has not acknowledged either. Over the same days Trump said a decision on renewed strikes was days away, and Iran's parliament took up a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A bet on whether the Bab el-Mandeb, the strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa that joins the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden, closes to shipping by year's end. Most Suez-bound traffic from Asia passes through it.
poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.recent: The Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, a short run up the coast from the strait, and oil jumped the same week. The fighting had reached the shipping lane this contract is about. Nothing reported since explains why traders later backed away from a closure.

poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if crude oil sets a new all-time price high before its deadline. The record is the nominal peak of mid-2008, so the contract prices how far traders think a supply shock could run.
poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.recent: Bets on a record jumped after the Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, and oil rose with them. The same jump raised the odds of a Fed hike. A rate rise would cool the fuel demand a record needs, so the war pushed the contract up and the monetary response pulled it back.

poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the ruling party that has held a majority in the State Duma since 2003, comes first in every one of Russia's regions. It settles No if a single region goes to another party.
poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.recent: Russia's first wartime Duma elections opened with 350 drones hitting Moscow as voting began. Two days later, another Ukrainian drone strike on the capital killed a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man. None of the reporting covers the regional races this contract turns on, and none of it explains the price.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran reach a ceasefire by September 25. Its price, in cents on the dollar, is what traders will pay for that outcome.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Tehran put terms in writing: seven conditions to end the war went to Washington via Qatar, and Ghalibaf said Iran's Hormuz terms had been conveyed as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. Against that, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker, and Trump said a war decision was days away.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro, the Rio de Janeiro senator and eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders pay per dollar of payout.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: The only report in the fortnight about Flavio Bolsonaro himself pointed the other way: he was probed for corruption as the Brazil election tightened. Nothing else in the input explains why traders paid more for his win.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its benchmark interest rate unchanged at a given meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each inflation print and Fed signal.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Traders sold the hold once the war reached oil: Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, and Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call. The Fed then raised rates in a 12-0 vote, citing a closed strait and defying Trump's calls to lower rates, while the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5%, its highest since 2007.

poly-will-xi-jinping-visit-us-by-septemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China's leader Xi Jinping sets foot in the United States by September 23. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks the state of summit diplomacy between Washington and Beijing.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out only if Republicans win control of both the Senate and the House in the November 2026 US midterms. Its price is what traders will pay for a unified Republican Congress in Trump's final two years.

poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.standing: Kharg Island is Iran's main crude export terminal, in the northern Persian Gulf, and most of the country's oil leaves through it. The contract pays out if Iran loses control of the island by 31 December.
poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.recent: Escalation and diplomacy ran side by side. Trump said a war decision was days away. Iran sent 7 conditions to Washington via Qatar and conveyed its Hormuz terms as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. None of it touched Kharg Island itself.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves as the field of rivals takes shape.

stocks:HAL.NS.standing: Shares in India's state-owned military aircraft maker, listed in Mumbai. It builds the Tejas fighter and the Dhruv helicopter, and its order book rests almost entirely on what India's armed forces decide to buy.
stocks:HAL.NS.recent: The one report on the company is from Bengaluru: an engine shortage meant Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers it owed last fiscal year. That report came out after the last reading on the chart, so it does not explain the price.

stocks:HON.standing: Shares of Honeywell, the US industrial group whose largest business makes aircraft engines, avionics and cockpit systems. Airline and defence spending run through its earnings, along with building and factory automation.
stocks:HON.recent: The only Honeywell-related news in the window came from Bengaluru: Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers due last fiscal year because it was short of engines, and the aircraft depends on Honeywell for them. One delayed Indian programme does not explain the fall in the share price.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the channel for about a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, returns to normal by December 31. Its price is what traders pay for a yes.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Bets soured as the US-Iran war widened: Iranian strikes damaged US jets in Jordan, and a projectile killed a sailor off Qeshm Island, shelving the Muscat talks. Only three vessels transited Hormuz on Wednesday. Iran's terms for reopening the strait have since reached Washington through mediators, with Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi in Tehran.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, the US bill that would divide crypto oversight between the SEC and the CFTC, is signed into law this year. Stablecoin issuers, exchanges and token projects are all exposed to it.
poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.recent: A brief surge in the bill's odds on prediction markets reversed the next day, when Republicans rejected the Democrats' counter-proposal on the bill. Even during the rally, the bill was still described as facing a long road. Bitcoin slipped as the odds faded, which shows how closely crypto prices now follow the bill.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve lifts its policy rate by a quarter point at its October decision. That rate sets US borrowing costs, from mortgages to Treasuries, and the dollar's pull on everyone else.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: The betting built after the Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha and oil jumped, turning a war into an inflation problem. Goldman Sachs abandoned its no-hike call, the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5%, and the Fed then raised rates 12-0, defying Trump's calls to cut, so a second hike became something worth wagering on.

poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline resumes flow by 31 October. The line carries crude from the eastern oilfields to Red Sea terminals at Yanbu, and is the kingdom's main way to export oil without Hormuz.
poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.recent: Attacks shut the line, leaving Saudi Arabia without its only Hormuz bypass. The Houthis then declared "blockade for blockade" against Saudi Arabia, told Washington only Saudi-flagged vessels remain targets, and the US issued security alerts covering 10 Middle East countries.

poly-will-nicols-maduro-be-the-leader-of.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Nicolás Maduro still leads Venezuela when it settles. Its price is what traders will pay for his hold on power, which is tied to US sanctions, Venezuelan oil output and the opposition's pressure on Caracas.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Israel and Iran are under a ceasefire by 30 September. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Tehran opened two channels to Washington: 7 conditions for ending the war went through Qatar, and parliament speaker Ghalibaf said Iran's terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz had been conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. In the same days, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill reached the speaker.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Democratic Party wins a majority of the US House of Representatives in the November 2026 midterms. Whichever party holds the House controls federal spending bills and the power to impeach.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: The only American election news in the window was about the rules, not the voters: The Atlantic wrote that the Supreme Court recognised the danger of Trump's election plan, and a New York Times opinion piece asked whether the election would be stolen after all. Neither reports a poll or a race that accounts for the betting.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-sen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Democrat wins Ohio's 2026 special election for the US Senate seat JD Vance gave up to become vice president. It is a bet on whether a state that has trended Republican flips back.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built so that the sender, receiver and amount of every transfer are hidden by default. That privacy has pushed it off many regulated exchanges and made it a common currency for ransom demands.
xmr.recent: The hackers who breached Revolut and ranked 680 accounts by how much they held demanded $3 million in Monero in exchange for not selling the customer data. A ransom demand of that size is too small to move the coin's market, and nothing else in the fortnight's news accounts for the rise.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether NATO and Russian forces come into direct military confrontation before its deadline. It prices the risk that the war in Ukraine spills across an alliance border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: The trough came as a US envoy signalled momentum for Russia-Ukraine talks. Bets climbed back after a drone hit a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland, on a night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine, and again when a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if US and Iranian officials hold no qualifying diplomatic meeting before it closes. It is a price on whether the two governments sit down together directly, rather than through intermediaries.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Tehran is reaching Washington only through couriers. Its 7 conditions for ending the war went via Qatar, and Ghalibaf says its Hormuz terms were conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. At the same time, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker, and Trump says a war decision is days away.

poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Buttigieg, the former US transportation secretary, wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders will pay per dollar of payout on that outcome.

poly-will-the-next-claude-opus-model-be-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic ships a new Claude Opus model before its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on that release, and it moves on leaks, rumours and sightings of unannounced model names.

poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China invades Taiwan before 2026 ends, so its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. Chip supply chains and Pacific shipping lanes are exposed to the event it bets on.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if NATO and Russian forces clash militarily before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on incidents along the alliance's eastern border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.recent: The climb began the night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine and one struck a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland. Two days later a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania, which put alliance fire and Russian hardware in the same airspace.

poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Avigdor Lieberman becomes Israel's next prime minister. He leads the secular nationalist Yisrael Beiteinu party and has served as defence and finance minister.
poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.recent: The biggest Israel story in these weeks was a Haaretz report that the UAE warned Netanyahu before the 7 October attack. Netanyahu threatened legal action over the report. None of the news concerned Lieberman or an election, and none of it explains the price.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-ohio-s.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Republican wins Ohio's 2026 US Senate race, a special election for the seat JD Vance left to become vice-president. Ohio is one of the few seats Democrats must flip to take the chamber.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: Shares of Samsung Electronics on the Korea Exchange in Seoul. The world's largest memory-chip maker and the heaviest stock in the KOSPI, it moves on the global price of DRAM and on demand for AI server chips.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: The only Samsung news in the fortnight came from Suwon, where the company said it would double memory output and clean 50,000 glass carriers a month next year. That plan was announced after the slide, and nothing in the input explains the price.

stocks:PARA.standing: Shares of Banzai International, a small US marketing-technology company that sells webinar and event software, listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market. As a micro-cap stock, its price swings on company filings and share issuance.

stocks:WBD.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of the Warner Bros. film studio, HBO, CNN and the Discovery cable networks. Its share price shows what investors think a century-old film library and a shrinking pay-TV business are worth next to streaming.
stocks:WBD.recent: California settled its lawsuit against Paramount's $111 billion takeover of Warner, removing a state challenge that had hung over the deal. Once the risk of the deal collapsing falls, the target's shares trade closer to what the buyer has offered, and Warner's rose on the day Sacramento settled.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: Shares in Google's parent company, traded on Nasdaq. Search advertising still pays for most of the business, so the price moves with ad spending, antitrust rulings and how investors judge its AI and cloud bets.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Google's news this fortnight was about security and spending, not earnings: a €13 billion data-centre commitment in Finland, a Chrome exploit shared by four China-linked hacking groups, and Gemini breaching three companies in a safety test. None of it accounts for the share price.

poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI models, reaches a $3 trillion valuation by its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on frontier-AI valuations climbing that far.
poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touched Anthropic's funding or valuation. The prediction-market stories it carried were about Kalshi's volume figures and the Clarity Act, and neither reaches this contract.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats hold a majority of the US Senate after the November 2026 midterms. Senate control decides whether a president's judges, cabinet picks and treaties get confirmed.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: The only US election news in the window was about how the vote will be run, not about who is winning. The Atlantic wrote that the Supreme Court recognised the danger of Trump's election plan, but nothing names a Senate race, candidate or poll that would explain the shift.

poly-will-nithya-raman-win-the-2026-los-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Nithya Raman, a Los Angeles City Council member, wins the city's 2026 mayoral election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it runs against the incumbent's own contract.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Vladimir Putin stops being Russia's president before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome: a running bet on a leader who has held power since 1999.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: Russia held its first wartime Duma elections, with 350 drones hitting Moscow as voting opened, and the results showed Putin's party winning. Two days later, a second mass drone attack on the capital killed two people and set fire to a refinery supplying 40% of the city's fuel, but the vote went ahead.

stocks:VZ.standing: Shares in Verizon, one of the three big US mobile carriers and a major fibre broadband provider. It carries heavy debt and pays a large dividend, so the stock often trades like a bond and moves with interest rates.

stocks:META.standing: Shares in the company that owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, listed on the Nasdaq. Almost all of its revenue comes from advertising, so the price follows ad spending and how much investors will fund its AI spending.
stocks:META.recent: Meta launched Muse, an AI agent that can send emails, book travel and work through WhatsApp, and the shares jumped 5% as it was pitched against Google. A week later Zuckerberg distanced Meta from calls for an AI slowdown. Then Amazon blocked Muse from shopping on its platform, the first big fight over which AI agents can buy on a user's behalf.

stocks:AMZN.standing: Shares of Amazon, listed on Nasdaq. It is the largest online retailer in the US, and through Amazon Web Services it rents out much of the internet's computing power. That cloud business earns most of its operating profit.
stocks:AMZN.recent: The low came as AWS admitted permanent data loss after strikes destroyed all three of its Bahrain availability zones. Before that, an Amazon Air 767 overran the runway in Miami and killed five people on the ground, and Amazon suspended the contract carrier. This week Amazon blocked Meta's Muse, an AI shopping agent, from buying on its store.

stocks:WMT.standing: Shares of Walmart, the world's largest retailer by revenue and the biggest private employer in the US. Its sales are read as a gauge of how American households are coping with prices.

stocks:2330.TW.standing: Shares of TSMC on the Taiwan Stock Exchange. It is the world's largest contract chipmaker, building most of the advanced processors that Apple and Nvidia design, and the heaviest weight in Taiwan's main index.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazil's incumbent president, wins the 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: The one Brazilian story in the fortnight was a corruption probe into Flavio Bolsonaro as the Brazil election tightened. That news lands on the rival camp, not on Lula, and nothing else in the input explains why traders marked his chances down.

poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran hold talks by the end of October 2026. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, for that outcome.
poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.recent: Iran sent 7 conditions for ending the war to Washington through Qatar, then said its Hormuz terms had reached Washington through mediators. The US had just given Iran's president a visa for UN meetings in New York. At the same time, Trump said a war decision was days away, and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill sat with Tehran's speaker.

poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays $1 if Republicans win a majority of the US House in the 2026 midterms. Its price is what bettors will pay for that outcome. The House controls federal spending and can impeach.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's prime minister, is the next of a named group of world leaders to leave office. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Iran's leadership changes hands before the year ends. It shows what traders will pay on a break at the top of a system where the supreme leader, not the elected president, has the final say.
poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.recent: Tehran spent the fortnight acting as a sitting government: it sent seven conditions for ending the war to Washington through Qatar, filed a bill to leave the Non-Proliferation Treaty, and its president received a US visa for the UN meetings in New York. Trump said a decision on new strikes was days away. None of it touched who rules Iran.

wiki-nigeria.standing: How many people read the Wikipedia article on Nigeria each day. Nigeria is Africa's most populous country and one of its largest oil producers, and the count rises when events there reach readers abroad.
wiki-nigeria.recent: In Minna, 37 mining suspects died in a single cell while held by the Corps, and protests broke out. Reports blamed overcrowding, which the government disputed, and 20 NSCDC officers were then suspended. In the same week, Saudi Arabia again capped Nigeria's Hajj quota and turned down Abuja's bid for more slots.

stocks:BABA.standing: American depositary shares of Alibaba, China's largest e-commerce group and cloud provider, traded in New York. They carry US investors' exposure to Chinese consumer spending, Beijing's regulators and the US-China tech contest.
stocks:BABA.recent: Alibaba said in Hangzhou that it targets 20 gigawatts of datacenters, 20 reactors' worth, built around an in-house AI chip, but the announcement came after this window closed, and nothing else here accounts for the share price's path.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The dominant designer of the graphics processors that train and run AI models, locked in by its CUDA software. Its share price is the market's running bet on how much the big tech firms keep spending on datacenters.
stocks:NVDA.recent: The month's Nvidia news cut against its China business: Washington capped its compute sales to China ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, Alibaba committed to its own AI chip, and Shanghai's Enflame tripled on debut. None of it explains the rise, which had run its course before these stories broke.

stocks:GLXY.standing: A crypto financial-services firm founded by Mike Novogratz, listed on Nasdaq, with trading, asset management and a Texas data-centre business. Its shares tend to amplify bitcoin's moves.

stocks:NVO.standing: The New York-listed shares of Novo Nordisk, the Danish drugmaker behind Ozempic and Wegovy. Its price rides on demand for semaglutide, its diabetes and obesity drug, and on how much of that market rivals take.
stocks:NVO.recent: Nothing reported this fortnight explains the slide itself. Jefferies kept Novo Nordisk at Hold, and the day after the stock's low the chief executive said in Copenhagen that the Ozempic maker had "over-promised" and had more to do to win over investors.
